clue.text: Planet Earth's latterly devastated in places

indicators.note: the later of the two Earth letters in the word for places is wiped out, leaving the other

parts.note: venues are places where events are held

explanation.surface: A lament that the planet's ground has lately been laid waste in many spots.
explanation.walkthrough: 'latterly devastated' removes the second E from VENUES, not the first.
explanation.definitionFit: The second planet from the Sun, named for the Roman goddess of love.

clue.text: Prints of 'Vertigo' regularly include feature on Stewart up front

indicators.note: the alternate letters of the film title take the next pieces inside them
taking every other letter of the film title, starting from the second

parts.note: the chin is a facial feature

indicators.note: only the leading letter of the actor's name is used

explanation.surface: Posters of Hitchcock's Vertigo routinely show James Stewart's face prominently.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vertigo' and 'Stewart' paint Hitchcock's 1958 film, but the title is only a source of letters; 'regularly' takes its even letters, which then 'include' the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Etchings are prints made from plates incised with acid.

clue.text: See 27
States ignored rising star — a goddess!

indicators.note: in a down entry, rising means the remaining letters read upwards
the abbreviation for the States is left out of the star's name

parts.note: Sirius, the Dog Star, is the brightest star in the night sky
US is short for the United States

explanation.surface: America overlooks an up-and-coming celebrity who turns out to be divine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ignored' leaves SIRI from SIRIUS; 'rising' turns it upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Iris is the Greek goddess of the rainbow and messenger of the gods.

clue.text: Marry or divorce?

definitions.meaning: to cling to them, as a spouse does
to ... also means to split apart

explanation.surface: A blunt question about whether to wed or split.
explanation.definitionFit: This verb is a contronym: it means both cling together and split apart.

clue.text: Innate lateness I displayed

indicators.note: the letters are laid out in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone confessing that their tardiness is part of their nature.
explanation.definitionFit: Something essential is inherent, belonging to the very nature of a thing.

clue.text: Cast in audition, Mrs Sharples trains for big occasion …

indicators.note: the word is heard rather than read, so a same-sounding spelling is used

parts.note: cast means thrown, or sent
Ena Sharples was the hairnetted battleaxe of the British TV soap Coronation Street
RY is the abbreviation for railway

explanation.surface: A soap matriarch, chosen at an audition, rehearses for an important event.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cast in audition' looks theatrical, but it is the sound of SENT, spelt CENT.
explanation.definitionFit: A hundredth anniversary is a major commemorative event, here Sid James's.

clue.text: … hit she's made wearing top draped over singular vehicle for 11

indicators.note: the scrambled letters sit inside the garment, as if worn

parts.note: a blouse is a woman's top

indicators.note: the scrambled letters are wrapped around the single letter
the letters are made into a fresh order

parts.note: S is the grammatical abbreviation for singular

explanation.surface: A hit song has a woman in a draped top riding in one vehicle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'made' rearranges HIT SHE'S; it wraps S and sits inside BLOUSE.
explanation.definitionFit: A 1970s British sitcom starring Sid James, i.e. a showcase for him.

clue.text: Quote from a dead leader

parts.note: Il Duce, the leader, was Mussolini's title

explanation.surface: A citation taken from a deceased head of state.
explanation.definitionFit: To adduce is to cite as evidence, as one quotes a source.

clue.text: A measure of concealment?

parts.note: an old dry measure, and the vessel under which you hide your light in the proverb

explanation.surface: Asking how much something is hidden.
explanation.definitionFit: This unit of dry volume is also the container in the saying about hiding your light.

clue.text: Comic actor's side-splitting spot on square — it's his 7 today!

indicators.note: the word side is split open to take the next piece

parts.note: taken as written
a spot is a predicament, a jam

explanation.surface: Praise for a hilarious comedian bang on time for his anniversary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'side-splitting' looks like praise for the comedy, but 'splitting' is the container signal acting on 'side'. The tail 'it's his 7 today' points to his centenary.
explanation.definitionFit: Sid James was a British comedian of the Carry On films, born in 1913.

clue.text: 11's role in 27,3 — opposite no maiden!

indicators.note: the maiden's letter is not there, so it is taken away

parts.note: an antonym is a word of opposite meaning
M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over

explanation.surface: An actor's part described as the very contrary of a young woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Sid James played Mark Antony in the 1964 Carry On film set in Rome and Egypt.

clue.text: Lad's unconscious in midst of mayhem

indicators.note: the next piece goes inside the central pair
the central pair of letters is taken from the word

parts.note: someone knocked out is out cold

explanation.surface: A boy lies senseless in the middle of chaos.
explanation.walkthrough: 'midst of' takes the central two letters of the six-letter word, not a single middle letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A youth is a young man, much the same as a lad.

clue.text: Comfortable with 'Our Party', Miliband's almost premier

parts.note: we would call our own party us
Ed Miliband was the Labour leader in 2013

indicators.note: the last letter is dropped

parts.note: premier means top, first

explanation.surface: A political slogan suggesting Miliband nearly became Prime Minister.
explanation.walkthrough: 'premier' looks like Prime Minister but means TOP, cut short by 'almost'.
explanation.definitionFit: To be accustomed to something is to be at ease with it.

clue.text: Daily subverted congenital cheat

parts.note: a daily, or char, is a cleaning woman who comes in each day

indicators.note: turned upside down, so in a down entry the letters read upwards

parts.note: natal means from birth

explanation.surface: A newspaper undermined by a born swindler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Daily' looks like a newspaper but is a cleaner, CHAR; NATAL turned up gives LATAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A charlatan is a fraud or impostor, one who cheats others.

clue.text: See 8
See 8
Snag involving electronic industrial design

indicators.note: the snag wraps round the next letter

parts.note: a hitch is a snag or problem

explanation.surface: A glitch in some electronic machinery design.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an architectural and design style that flaunts industrial materials and technology.

clue.text: Swallowing cold 'economy' banger

indicators.note: the cold letter is consumed and disappears

parts.note: economy class is cheap
C is the tap abbreviation for cold

explanation.surface: A cut-price sausage being gulped down cold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'banger' is British slang for a sausage, but here it means an old car.
explanation.definitionFit: A heap is slang for a decrepit old car, just like a banger.

clue.text: See 24
Like lovers in a forest — beginning to tremble?

parts.note: the Forest of Arden is the setting of As You Like It

indicators.note: only the first letter is used

explanation.surface: Couples in Shakespeare's woods start to quiver with passion.
explanation.definitionFit: Lovers are passionate, which is what this adjective means.

clue.text: Flamenco rendition collects repeat performance

indicators.note: the phrase gathers up the letters within it, running across the two words

explanation.surface: A flamenco performance gathers a call for more.
explanation.definitionFit: An encore is an extra performance demanded by the audience.

clue.text: It's a feather in one's cap to have broken-down sheep sold off

definitions.text: It's a feather in one's cap

indicators.note: the animals are disposed of, so taken away

parts.note: ramshackle means tumbledown, dilapidated
rams are male sheep

explanation.surface: An achievement worth boasting of: offloading some worn-out livestock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a feather in one's cap' is an idiom for an achievement; here read literally.
explanation.definitionFit: A hackle is a plume of neck feathers worn in some Highland soldiers' bonnets.

clue.text: Covet neighbour's superior chicken

parts.note: to crave is to covet

indicators.note: in a down entry, the top letter is placed above

explanation.surface: The commandment against coveting the neighbour's prize hen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chicken' looks like the neighbour's bird but means cowardly.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words are adjectives meaning cowardly.

clue.text: 11's paramour touring Mile End — with similar ladies?

indicators.note: the name goes round the next letter

parts.note: Barbara Windsor, known as Babs, was Sid James's lover

indicators.note: the final letter of the word is taken

explanation.surface: Sid's lover travels round East London's Mile End with a gang of girls.
explanation.walkthrough: Mile End is an East London district; 'End' takes its last letter, E.
explanation.definitionFit: Babes are girls in the mould of the Carry On star, playful wordplay on her name.

clue.text: It's hot: a shock launch for new programme featuring 11

parts.note: H is the tap abbreviation for hot

indicators.note: the letters are made new by rearrangement

explanation.surface: A surprise launch for a fresh TV show starring the comic.
explanation.definitionFit: A British radio and TV comedy series in which Sid James co-starred with Tony Hancock.

clue.text: Sally's first child's a runner

indicators.note: only the opening letter is taken

parts.note: a kid is a child

explanation.surface: Sally's eldest is an athlete.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a runner' looks like an athlete but is a sledge or aircraft runner.
explanation.definitionFit: A skid is a runner on which a helicopter or sledge rests.

clue.text: Group of slapdash ramraiders in retreat

indicators.note: a run of letters is grouped within the words

explanation.surface: A careless gang of smash-and-grab raiders falls back.
explanation.definitionFit: An ashram is a religious retreat or hermitage in India.

clue.text: Sign on motor — 'Dreadfully Corny Classical Comedy!'

indicators.note: the sign is placed on, or after, the other pieces

parts.note: a motor is a car

indicators.note: the word is badly mangled into a new order

parts.note: Leo is a sign of the zodiac

explanation.surface: A sticker on a car mocking a feeble period comedy.
explanation.definitionFit: Carry On Cleo (1964) is a Carry On comedy set in ancient Rome and Egypt.

clue.text: Ending and one French piece of dialogue tweaked

parts.note: fin is French for end
et is French for and
une is French for one (feminine)

indicators.note: just the first letter is taken

explanation.surface: A French script whose ending and a piece were adjusted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'French' governs Ending, and, one: FIN, ET, UNE.
explanation.definitionFit: Fine-tuned means adjusted precisely, just as tweaked is.
